title: The Stone Vault Turns to Light
brief: Original Romantic pipe-organ toccata for one organist in a large church; running hands above a striding pedal theme, quiet flute middle, D-major full-organ return.

sections.intent: Manual figure opens above a tonic pedal; dominant intake
Pedal theme in three eight-bar paragraphs; D minor, half cadence then tonic
Fragment and transpose the stride through chromatic mediants; dominant return
Stopped-flute cantilena in B-flat; two hands, restrained pedal; quiet centre
Recover the figure, then full left manual; prepare the major-mode return
D-major transformation, wider register and faster left hand, full-organ accumulation
Minor-subdominant recollection, final dominant, fourteen-beat major chord and release

tracks.name: Pedal - striding theme at sounding pitch

decisions: Romantic primary: chromatic-mediant development, modal mixture, rubato, transformed return and broad dynamic contrast.
Borrow Baroque rhythm only for continuous motor figuration, and timbre only for pipe organ; this is a ternary toccata, without fugal exposition, imitative entries or a borrowed model.
Theme first: D2 dotted half, F2 quarter | F2 half, D2 half | E2 dotted half, G2 quarter | A1 dotted half, C#2 quarter. Each is checked against its authored harmony.
Organ dynamics come from fixed registrations, texture and declared expression-level automation; key velocity is fixed and does not control the organ.
One player, two manual hands and monophonic pedal. The low thematic line is foreground; manual figuration deliberately lies above it.
The church response and C80 target are a design choice, not a claim about an actual building or a listening judgement.
The final chord holds fourteen quarter beats at 70 BPM, followed by two beats of written rest and eight seconds of tail.
r1 Q1/Q2 kept: velocity is intentionally fixed at 96 because all three registrations ignore velocity. Timing, articulation, registration and expression-level automation carry phrasing.
r1 Q3 changed: selected low D3/E3 manual tones move up an octave at each of the 17 flagged locations, leaving the pedal theme intact.

r1 Q4 kept: exposition and development intentionally retain motor density; development changes harmonic region to F-sharp minor, C major and F minor/flat-side harmony, raises the right-hand register, fragments pedal statements and changes tempo.
r1 Q5 changed: middle-section left-hand chords now enter as four distinct phrase gestures, with different note releases; the fourth bar retains a chordal cadence.
r3: same-key events shared by both full-manual tracks are reassigned to the nearest lower chord tone in the left hand. This avoids treating one pipe rank as two independent instruments on those keys.

r4: r1/r2 measurements put the coda about 7.4 LU above the returning section and held master gain 2.8 dB below target. Shape the written late-section automation to spread the arrival across the return and coda, leaving wide dynamics and the long final chord intact.

authorship.method: Every note written by compose.py, with explicit harmony and manually designed theme, figure cells and form.
authorship.sample_bank: Installed VCSL organ build b2; CC0 samples

revision_history.change: First complete authored score and registration-aware bus mix.

Manual-support clarity: lift the 17 questioned low-interval locations; stagger and vary the stopped-flute left-hand chord entries/releases. Keep velocity and exposition/development density with documented reasons.
Remove ten duplicate full-manual key presses between the two hands; retain right-hand figures and pedal pitches.

Broaden the return crescendo after bar 81, reaching the increased levels at bars 89-97, then compensate the much denser final manual chord by 3 dB and its pedal by 1 dB relative to r3. Also complete the two-hand audit at b19: move the replacement D4 to A3, since D4 met the preceding RH sixteenth. All other score events and the quiet centre are unchanged.
